rome.titre: Following in Rome's Footsteps in Africa
rome.soustitre: The Great Roman Cities, by Le Kef
rome.note: Be realistic: don't try to cram everything into one day. Combining Bulla Regia and Dougga (with a stop in Béja) on the first day is doable but will take a long time—leave Tunis early (around 7 a.m.). Spend the night in Le Kef.

etapes.note: In the morning: the underground villas and their mosaics. Lunch is available in Béja along the way.
Afternoon. Large site (at least 2 hours): combined with Bulla Regia on the same day, it’s a busy day.

etapes.sejour: 2 nights — set aside a full day for Le Kef
etapes.note: Overnight stay in Kef (required). The medina, the kasbah, Sicca Veneria, museums: a full day of exploration.
Day trip from Le Kef: Roman baths on the banks of the Mellègue wadi. Accessible by car via a small road/dirt track—proceed with caution in rainy weather.
Drive from Le Kef; arrival at the Capitoline Temple at the end of the day.
The last stop before heading back: the amphitheater, one of the best-preserved in the world.

pepites.nom: Arc de Gordien III (Musti / El Krib)
pepites.note: Just a stone's throw from Dougga: the monumental arch of ancient Musti, on the main road between Carthage and Theveste.

pepites.nom: Marche romain (macellum) de Musti / El Krib
pepites.note: The market (macellum) at Musti, still visible today. The present-day town of El Krib still holds a market (day to be confirmed on site).

carthage.soustitre: From Byrsa to the Ports: The City of Hannibal

pepites.note: Punic Houses on the Slopes of Byrsa: The City's Urban Planning Before 146 B.C.
On Byrsa Hill: stelae, sarcophagi, and Punic artifacts.

ksour.soustitre: Hilltop Villages and Fortified Granaries of Tataouine

etapes.note: There are many Berber guesthouses and bed-and-breakfasts around Tataouine—a chance to spend a night in a restored ksar.

pepites.note: Restored ksar north of Tataouine — also a filming location for *Star Wars* (Episode I).

cinema.soustitre: Southern Film Locations: From the Chott to the Ksour

etapes.nom: Ong Jmel / Mos Espa (decor Star Wars)
etapes.note: Early in the morning to enjoy the light and the cool air (in the middle of the desert).

etapes: Ferme des Lars / dome (Chott el-Djerid, pres de Nefta)

etapes.nom: Hotel Sidi Driss (decor Star Wars, ferme des Lars)
etapes.note: You can stay at the cave hotel itself (the Lars' farm from the movie) or at a guesthouse in Matmata.

pepites.note: A spectacular hilltop Berber village, one of the most photogenic in the South.

tozeur.soustitre: Brick Medina, Oasis, and Salt Sea, departing from Tozeur
tozeur.note: The cool of the morning at Chott el-Djerid (lights and mirages); the afternoon in the shade of the palm groves. Water, a hat, and a full tank of gas before heading into the desert.

etapes.note: The old neighborhood with its ochre-colored brick facades featuring geometric patterns—best explored on foot.
A traditional oasis at the edge of the Chott, on the road to Kébili.

etapes.nom: Ferme des Lars / dome (Chott el-Djerid, pres de Nefta)
etapes.note: The Great Salt Sea; the cinema dome near Nefta. Stunning at sunset—then spend the night in Tozeur or Nefta.

etapes.nom: Ong Jmel / Mos Espa (decor Star Wars)
etapes.note: Day 2, early morning: the vast desert to the northwest—the setting for Mos Espa. Access via dirt road—4×4 or guided tour recommended.

pepites.via: Ferme des Lars / dome (Chott el-Djerid, pres de Nefta)
pepites.note: A frontier oasis in the far west, on the edge of the chott—a peaceful corner of the world.

douz.soustitre: Saharan oases and the Great Erg, starting from Douz
douz.note: The major event in the Sahara is the Douz International Sahara Festival (usually in late December—check the dates for that year): camel races, poetry, and music. For desert activities (camel treks, camping), go with a local guide. Water and sun: exercise caution.

etapes.sejour: 1 night in Douz (hotel) or camping in the dunes
etapes.note: The camel treks set off for the dunes west of Douz. Evening: sunset over the erg, followed by a camp under the stars or a stay at a hotel in Douz.
A peaceful Saharan oasis in the heart of the desert.
The last oasis before the great erg—it feels like the end of the world.
A traditional oasis on the road leading up to Kébili.
A small oasis on the edge of the chott.
The historic oasis capital of Nefzaoua, with its markets and palm groves.

pepites.note: A Roman fort in the middle of the desert, on the edge of the erg—4x4 vehicle and a guide are required.

gafsa.titre: Gafsa: From the Capsian Period to the Mining Basin
gafsa.soustitre: An Ancient Oasis, Prehistory, and a Mining Epic
gafsa.note: Gafsa gave its name to the Capsian, a major prehistoric culture. In the afternoon, head to the mining basin and the Seldja Gorges on the Red Lizard Train (check the schedule).

etapes.note: The ancient pools fed by springs, in the heart of the city.
Just a stone's throw from the pools, in the old town.
Mosaics and collections from the region.
The eponymous Capsien site, north of Gafsa. Overnight in Gafsa; tomorrow, we're heading to the mining basin.
Day 2: The historic capital of the phosphate industry and the starting point of the mining train.

etapes.nom: Le Lezard Rouge (train historique de Metlaoui)
etapes.note: The restored Beylical train travels through the Seldja Gorge—check the schedule.

pepites.note: Oasis to the east, both a prehistoric site and a battlefield from 1943.
In the heart of the coal-mining region, a city steeped in working-class history (the 2008 uprising).

kef.titre: Le Kef, the balcony of the high plains
kef.soustitre: Kasbah, Sicca Veneria, and the Roman Baths
kef.note: The town is best explored on foot (there are some hills); save the trip to Hammam Mellègue for a half-day excursion when the weather is nice.

etapes.note: The hilltop medina and its narrow streets, with a view of the plains.
The Ottoman fortress that overlooks the city.
Remains of the Numidian and later Roman city, beneath the present-day city.

etapes.nom: Basilique Saint-Pierre (Dar El Kous, Le Kef)
etapes.note: A remarkably well-preserved early Christian church.
A domed sanctuary, a jewel of local religious art. Overnight in Kef; tomorrow, the Hammam Mellègue excursion.
Day 2, western excursion: Roman baths along the wadi. Road/dirt road—use caution in rainy weather.

pepites.note: A Numidian and Roman city south of Kef, featuring a theater and mosaics.
A stopover town on the way to Dougga, featuring arches and oil mills.

djerba.titre: Djerba, the island of mosques and souks
djerba.soustitre: Houmt Souk, La Ghriba, Djerbahood, and Ibadite villages
djerba.note: You can explore the island at a leisurely pace on a loop route, either by bike or by car. The Ghriba pilgrimage takes place in the spring (dates vary). Please respect places of worship (appropriate attire, silence).

etapes.note: The island's capital: souks, fondouks, and old warehouses.

etapes.nom: Borj El Kebir (Borj Ghazi Mustapha, Djerba)
etapes.note: The Spanish-Ottoman fort at the port of Houmt Souk.
A former Jewish quarter that has become the mural art village known as “Djerbahood.”
One of the oldest synagogues in the world, located in Erriadh. Overnight stay in Djerba (Houmt Souk or the Midoun area).
Day 2: A squat, white Ibadite mosque, typical of the island.
The potters' village, in the southern part of the island.

pepites.note: Port des Éponges in the southwest—also known as Mos Eisley in *Star Wars*.
The Roman road connecting the island to the mainland.

zarzis.titre: Zarzis, Gightis, and the ksours of Médenine
zarzis.soustitre: From the Gulf of Bou Ghrara to the fortified granaries
zarzis.note: Spend the morning along the coast (olive groves and lagoon), then head inland in the afternoon to visit the ksour. The southern border region may include restricted areas—check with local authorities.

etapes.note: A coastal town nestled among olive groves, on the site of ancient Gergis.
A major Roman port on the Gulf of Bou Ghrara, with a forum and thermal baths.
On the edge of the lagoon, just a stone's throw from Gightis and the Djerba causeway. Return to Zarzis (or nearby Djerba) for the night.
Day 2: The city of the ksour, ancient multi-story communal granaries.
A well-preserved fortified ksar, west of Médenine.

pepites.note: Another fortified granary in the region, with rows of ghorfas.

sousse.titre: Sousse, the Pearl of the Sahel
sousse.soustitre: The Medina, Ribat, and Catacombs of Hadrumet
sousse.note: You can explore the heart of the medina (the ribat, the Great Mosque, and the kasbah) on foot in a morning; spend the afternoon visiting the catacombs and, time permitting, take a trip to the Sahel.

etapes.note: A medieval fortified town listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Aghlabid monastery-fortress, climb up to the watchtower.
A austere 9th-century mosque, resembling a citadel.
The citadel that houses the museum and its mosaics.
In the kasbah: one of the country's most beautiful collections of mosaics.
Early Christian galleries carved out beneath the city.

pepites.note: A charming white village perched on a cliff to the north, on the site of a Roman warehouse.
A Berber village perched on a rocky outcrop to the northwest, with a sweeping view of the Sahel.

hammamet.soustitre: The Kasbah, Roman sites, and Punic Kerkouane
hammamet.note: Visit the kasbah and the old town in the morning; then head up the Cap Bon peninsula toward Nabeul and on to Kerkouane, a Punic gem, at the end of the route (allow half a day for the trip).

etapes.note: The fort overlooking the sea and the white-washed alleys of the medina.
A restored traditional home, embodying the Cap Bon way of life.
Roman site between Hammamet and Nabeul, necropolis and mosaics.
The ancient Punic and later Roman city, with its salt-curing workshops.
Punic and Roman collections from the region. Overnight on the coast (Hammamet / Nabeul); tomorrow, we’ll head north toward Kerkouane.
Day 2: The only Punic city to have survived intact—a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The highlight of the tour.

pepites.note: A fortress overlooking the sea, from Roman times to the Hafsid dynasty.
A Punic-Roman place of worship, from which the famous statue of Baal originates.

monastir.titre: Monastir and the Ribats of the Sahel
monastir.soustitre: Ribat, Bourguiba's Mausoleum, and Ancient Leptiminus
monastir.note: Visit the ribat and the old city in the morning; then head down to Lamta (ancient Leptiminus) and its museum. The ribats of Monastir and Sousse stretch from one end of the Sahel to the other.

etapes.note: The oldest ribat in the Maghreb, with superb views from Nador.
A simple mosque adjoining the ribat.
The medieval walls of the old town.
The gilded mausoleum of the first president, in the Sidi El Mezri Cemetery.
A sanctuary and necropolis adjacent to the mausoleum. Overnight in Monastir; tomorrow, Lamta and ancient Leptiminus.
Day 2: Lamta (Leptiminus), an Aghlabid ribat south of Monastir.
Collections from ancient Leptiminus, a port that was first Punic and later Roman.

pepites.note: Site of the Battle of Thapsus (46 B.C.) between Caesar and the Pompeians.
A representative of the Jewish community of the Sahel, in Moknine.

medina-classique.titre: La Médina de Tunis — le cœur classique
medina-classique.soustitre: Zitouna, souks et palais, à pied au fil des ruelles
medina-classique.note: Parcours à pied — comptez ~3 h en flânant. La médina est un labyrinthe : se perdre fait partie du plaisir, les plus belles trouvailles sont dans les ruelles secondaires. Matins en semaine = moins de monde. À goûter en chemin : brik (œuf-thon frit), lablabi (pois chiches, harissa, cumin), makroud (semoule-dattes-miel), bambalouni (beignet). Adresses réputées, à vérifier sur place : Dar Slah, El Ali, Ouled Ahmed (lablabi).

etapes.note: Les parfumeurs : eau de fleur d'oranger, jasmin, eau de rose. L'un des plus anciens souks, sur le chemin de la Zitouna.
Les bonnets de feutre rouge, artisanat vieux de plusieurs siècles — gestes encore visibles en atelier.
Café depuis le XVIIe siècle (~1630), terrasse avec vue sur le minaret de la Zitouna : le moment thé à la menthe. Horaires à vérifier sur place.

pepites.note: Palais beylical à patio, l'un des plus raffinés de la médina (siège de l'INP).
Grande demeure du XVIIIe, aujourd'hui maison de la médina — superbe enfilade de salles.

medina-nord.titre: La Médina populaire — Bab Souika & Halfaouine
medina-nord.soustitre: Cafés chantants, place animée et marché de la fripe
medina-nord.note: Le nord populaire de la médina — l'âme vivante de Tunis, loin des circuits touristiques. Bab Souika fut le haut lieu des « cafés chantants » et du chant soufi (ensemble Sulâmiyya) ; la place Halfaouine, immortalisée par le cinéma de Boughedir, vibre de ses souks ; la Hafsia, ancien quartier juif, abrite le marché de la fripe. Le quartier se vit surtout le soir — magique pendant le Ramadan (« Layali Bab Souika », concerts gratuits en plein air, zlabia chaude). À goûter : lablabi, fricassé, et la zlabia des nuits de Ramadan.

etapes.note: L'un des deux souks qui animent la place Halfaouine — épices, produits du quotidien, ambiance populaire.

pepites.note: Quartier voisin au nom lié au miel (la « Rue du Miel ») et à la mosquée El Borj.

medina-musees.soustitre: L'art de vivre tunisois derrière les murs
medina-musees.note: Pousser les portes discrètes des grandes demeures de la médina : derrière des façades sobres se cachent patios de marbre, plafonds peints et stucs ciselés. Les palais ne se visitent pas tous, mais plusieurs sont ouverts (musées, maisons de la médina, sièges culturels).

pepites.note: L'ensemble officiel (Primature, mosquée de la Kasbah) : ne se visite pas, mais beau de l'extérieur.

medina-nuit.soustitre: Cafés, lanternes, malouf et soirées de fête
medina-nuit.note: La médina se vit aussi la nuit. Ruelles éclairées de lanternes, parfums d'oud et de jasmin, cafés où l'on s'attarde autour d'un thé. Pendant le Ramadan, elle s'embrase : malouf, tarab et chants soufis, zlabia chaude, et le Festival de la Médina (30 soirées de concerts dans les palais, dont les nuits « Layali Slimania » à la Médersa). À vivre de préférence un soir de Ramadan.

etapes.note: Une des rues emblématiques des cafés du soir, près de la Zitouna.
Café depuis ~1630 : terrasse vue minaret, narguilé et musique andalouse le week-end.

pepites.note: Place vivante le soir, à deux pas de Bab Souika.

medina-jour.soustitre: Le meilleur du cœur classique et du nord populaire
medina-jour.note: Une journée complète pour embrasser la médina sans courir : le matin, le cœur classique (Zitouna, souks, palais) ; l'après-midi, le nord populaire (Bab Souika, Halfaouine, Hafsia). Prévoir une pause déjeuner (lablabi, brik) et un thé en terrasse.

pepites.note: Palais beylical raffiné (INP).
Le quartier du miel et la mosquée El Borj.
